messages:
jen: heads up — customer acme-prod hitting 503s during traffic spike, looks like Dedicated pool didn't scale up quick enough. root req ids: req-8a2f... happened ~08:15am PT. Anyone else seeing slow warmup?

marcus: saw similar alerts from metrics — GPU allocation lagged; autoscaler didn't launch nodes for ~45s, minReplicas set to 1, max 20.

sasha: can you paste the autoscaler events and the controller logs? Also which model and image size? Warmup time depends on model weight.

jen: model: gpt-3-small-quant, image: rw-infer:v2.6, customer load pattern: burst 500 rps for 30s. Repro steps:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/dedicated/acme -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -d '{ \"prompt\": \"token test\" }'
We saw 429 then 503s. Attaching snippet of HPA events:

```
kubectl describe hpa rw-dedicated-acme
Events:
  08:14:12  Scale up from 1 to 2 due to target CPU utilization
  08:15:00  Pending: creating pod rw-infer-12
  08:15:40  Pod rw-infer-12 failed to become ready: image pull 20s, init container 15s, model load 10s
```

marcus: those timings add up. Preflight quota checks also added ~5s. Any recent infra deploys?

infra-bot: [deploy] rw-runtime v2.6 rolled to us-west-2 at 07:58 — 40 nodes updated.

sasha: suspect two things: image pull + model load. For dedicated pools we have warm pool/idle instances feature — check if it's enabled for this customer. If not, increasing minReplicas to 2 or enabling warm pool hedges.

jen: warm pool is off for acme (they opted out for cost). What about autoscaler policy? current: stabilize window 300s, scale-up limit 1 per 30s.

marcus: that's the issue — scale-up rate is throttled. For bursty traffic, the policy is too conservative. Suggest policy change: allow up to 4 pods per 30s for dedicated tier or set burst_capacity to 3. Can we change per-customer override?

sasha: yes, we can apply per-namespace annotation: `autoscaler.redwood.io/scale-rate: \"4\"` — deployment-time change. Short-term mitigation: bump minReplicas to 3 for this customer.

jen: trying patch now.

jen: patched annotation + minReplicas=3. Monitoring... load spike incoming in 2m.

oncall: FYI there was a background job that evicted images from nodes yesterday to reclaim disk — might have increased image-pull times.

jen: after patch we still saw a ~12s delay due to model load; overall reduced 503s though. Need long-term: pre-pull models, warm pool, or faster model quantization. Product/ops — recommend defaults: warm_pool on for enterprise, or lower stabilize window.

marcus: agreed. I'll open infra ticket to enable pre-pull images in us-west-2 reserved fleet and propose new autoscaler defaults for dedicated customers. Also add a metric for 'effective_scale_time' measuring time from scale decision to endpoint readiness.

sasha: I'll add a config template for per-customer overrides and a runbook for oncall.

jen: I'll send customer note with RCA and temporary quota bump offer. Thanks all :thumbsup:

oncall: closing loop — will update incident if anything else pops.
thread_text_summary: Customer acme-prod saw 503s because Dedicated pool scaled too slowly; root cause combination: conservative autoscaler scale-rate, image pulls/model load, and an image eviction job. Short-term fixes: bump minReplicas, per-namespace scale-rate annotation. Long-term: pre-pull images, enable warm pool, adjust defaults and add metric for effective_scale_time.
